| [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) v2 | Two objects can agree on every probe in a restricted family without being isomorphic, so equivalence under a probe family is coarser than identity unless the family is rich enough | The general content of [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that it does not rest on [CLAIM-046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-046.md) and [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), which are about pragmatic identity. The restricted Yoneda functor is fully faithful exactly when the probe family is dense. A strong generator makes it conservative, which is weaker: a morphism the probes see as invertible is invertible, but objects with isomorphic profiles need not be isomorphic. Matching every probe's marginal leaves the joint unconstrained. The evidential rule is [CLAIM-322](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-322.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-265](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-265.md) v3 | Local descriptions that disagree are not thereby incompatible: whether they obstruct a joint description is decided only relative to a specified class of admissible correspondences between their observations, and a correspondence admitted only because it removes the disagreement decides nothing | The general content of [CLAIM-143](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the order of tests does not rest on [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), [CLAIM-004](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-004.md) and [CLAIM-035](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-035.md), which are about translation. Disagreement between local descriptions sorts into a coordinate difference, a structural transformation or a global obstruction, and the sort cannot be made until a class of admissible transition maps is given. Inertial frames ([CASE-039](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-039.md)) show disagreement with no obstruction once the maps are known. | Active |
| [CLAIM-267](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-267.md) v3 | Per-step discrepancies between a chain of maps and a reference chain compound through the sensitivity of the later steps, so the same local error can be damped, accumulated or amplified, and closeness at every step can coexist with large end-to-end divergence | The general content of [CLAIM-056](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-056.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the line-neutral recursion does not rest on [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s account of fidelity. It is elementary: with e_(i+1) ≤ L_i e_i + ε_i, the end-to-end error is bounded by the discrepancies weighted by the later Lipschitz constants. Three regimes follow. For stochastic kernels in total variation, contraction coefficients do not exceed one, so amplification needs another metric or a nonlinear, adaptive state. | Active |
| [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md) v6 | A regularized linear readout can tell apart only representations that differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed, so no such readout supplies a distinction beyond that symmetry | The general content of [CLAIM-193](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the linear result does not rest on [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), whose realist reading is about communicative identity. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). Kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed (THEORY-004, THEORY-723). An inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)). And spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). These are proved results for learned representations. | Active |
| [CLAIM-289](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-289.md) | Non-stochastic strings stay non-stochastic under total recursive models: their minimal randomness deficiency agrees with the finite-set one to within O(log n) in argument and value | The step that [THEORY-260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-260.md)'s promotion (version 2) names as the record's own: carrying [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md)'s non-stochastic strings, proved for finite-set models, to total recursive function models through Propositions B.1(b) and B.2(b) with Remark B.3. Remark B.3 asserts wholesale that every result of the paper extends to total functions up to a logarithmic term. This writes the extension out for this one result. It holds at O(log n) precision only, and does not reach [LIT-229](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-229.md)'s sophistication, which is defined at constant precision. | Active |

The book leaves this "as an exercise", and [NOTE-829](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-829.md) supplied the book's own proof of Thm 4.35, transferred. (b) The finite case that [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md) §5.3 states as known: XXᵀ = YYᵀ implies Y = XQ with Q orthogonal, with no assumption that the rows span R^d. With centring this becomes a translation and an orthogonal map. It does not say Q is unique, which fails when the rank is below d. | Active |
| [CLAIM-291](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-291.md) v2 | The adjoint of a square-integrable integral operator is the integral operator with the conjugate-transposed kernel | The record's own step, written down in [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md) and marked there as not the Riesz article's, which covers matrices and bounded operators only. For a kernel k in L²(μ⊗ν), the operator (Tf)(x) = ∫ k(x,y) f(y) dν(y) from L²(ν) to L²(μ) has adjoint (T*g)(y) = ∫ k̄(x,y) g(x) dμ(x), by Cauchy–Schwarz and Fubini. So T is self-adjoint, when μ = ν, exactly when k(x,y) = k̄(y,x) almost everywhere. It does not say where the symmetry of k comes from, which is [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md)'s question, and it is not claimed for kernels that are not square-integrable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) | Equivalence under feasible tests can be much coarser than statistical equivalence: there are ensembles almost disjoint from uniform that no polynomial-size test tells apart from it, and efficiently samplable ensembles of this kind exist if pseudorandom generators do | A15's witness for "Complexity changes what we mean by an observable", which the owner asked to have developed at U15, corrected by the reading of Goldreich (NOTE of 2026-10-15). The separation itself is unconditional: a counting argument gives ensembles supported on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform. Only an efficiently samplable witness needs an assumption, and a secure pseudorandom generator supplies one. All of it is asymptotic, about ensembles indexed by n. | Active |
| [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) v4 | A rendering can keep a distinction recoverable in principle and make it infeasible to recover: if pseudorandom generators exist, a uniformly random bit can be encoded so that an unbounded receiver recovers it except with probability at most 2⁻⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾, while no efficient receiver does non-negligibly better than chance | A14's first failure mode, computational inaccessibility, and A18's fourth candidate: "Recoverable in principle ≠ recoverable within budget." | [CLAIM-318](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-318.md) | Within a shared observational scenario, exact structure-preserving symmetries are the invertible members of a nested family of stochastic transports, and among Markov kernels between finite sets the invertible ones are the permutation matrices, so the invertible core is the relabellings, a groupoid in which objects joined by an arrow have isomorphic automorphism groups | Split from [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the nesting and its invertible core, stated on their own so that their warrant can be. For Markov kernels between finite sets, a stochastic matrix with a stochastic inverse is a permutation matrix, because a nonnegative matrix with a nonnegative inverse is monomial, so the invertible core is the relabellings. In that groupoid an invertible u : A → B gives Aut(A) ≅ Aut(B), which corrects A198 §8. It does not say what symmetries are for: that they supply the yardstick for non-symmetric transports is [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md)'s, and interpretive. | Active |
| [CLAIM-319](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-319.md) v2 | Over a scenario of n contexts in an odd cycle, changing the support of one context takes the contextual fraction from 1 to 0 while the other n − 1 contexts and every marginal are kept exactly, at a weighted observational distortion of 1/n, so within a scenario the fraction's Lipschitz constant against that distortion is at least n; and any change of global extension needs a contextual model on one side | Split from [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the derivation that claim called "decisive and checkable", stated on its own. It answers how small the local change can be; it says nothing about whether any data are contextual. | Active |
| [CLAIM-320](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-320.md) | Within one fixed measurement scenario, two no-signalling empirical models can agree on all but one of their contexts and on every single-observable marginal while their contextual fractions are 1 and 0, so keeping most local judgement distributions does not fix their global compatibility | Split from [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the possibility that claim's headline needs, shown by the pair it lost and recovered in [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). On the cover {AB, BC, AC} with binary outcomes, the parity triangle at 1/2 per allowed outcome is no-signalling and strongly contextual, with contextual fraction 1. Change only S_AC to {(0,0), (1,1)}: two contexts and every marginal are unchanged, and the model now extends to a global distribution, with fraction 0. It is an existence result by construction, and the weights are stipulated. | [CLAIM-345](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-345.md) v2 | Equal controllability rank does not fix the cost of control: for x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the least quadratic effort for a displacement Δ is Δ²/b², unbounded as b → 0 while the system stays controllable, and in general the least effort is Δxᵀ W_T^† Δx, set by the Gramian and not by its rank | A9 §2 and A12's Proposition 1 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, the step the owner's U9 "controllability of a system isn't binary" needs. For a scalar step x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the cheapest input costs Δ²/b², so two systems that are both controllable can differ in cost by any factor. Proved here because the record holds no source for it. The sharp edge: the cost is relative to a fixed input norm, and rescaling the input makes every b cost the same, so comparing costs across systems needs inputs in common units. | Active |

Three elementary constructions, each with one obstruction and not the others, are given in the body. | [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) v4 | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief | The owner's correction, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure." A37 granted it ("I agree with your correction") and built the acceptance sets, their intersection and the compatibility complex. Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. The definitional facts are shown in the body, including that every pair of demands can be jointly improvable while the triple is not. The sharp edge: relief compares complexes for the same declared demands, so a reorganization that deletes a demand is not compared at all, and two reorganizations can be incomparable. It is the move [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) made for translation, in a new line. | Active |
| [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md) v2 | A coarse-graining preserves a deterministic judgment exactly when the judgment is constant on its fibres: the judgment then factors through the coarse description, uniquely on its image, and otherwise two states the judgment tells apart have been merged | A21 §3 and §18 (Candidate 1) of the exchange of 2026-10-17, and A22's Construction A: for a judgment J and a coarse-graining C on the same states, J = j∘C for some j exactly when C(x₁) = C(x₂) implies J(x₁) = J(x₂). Granted, because it is elementary (the universal property of a quotient) and Ak's; the proof is in the body. | [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v4 | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. | [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) v3 | Whether several objectives share a strict first-order descent direction, 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, is invariant under smooth invertible reparameterization, while the sign of a Euclidean gradient inner product is not, and a negative inner product does not exclude common descent; a budgeted version is invariant only with the metric pulled back | A35 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U35 "double click" on whether functionally equivalent parameterizations give equivalent frustration diagnoses. Gradients transform as g′ = Jᵀg and directions as v′ = J⁻¹v, so directional derivatives, and with them the common-descent test 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, do not depend on coordinates. A Euclidean inner product does: g₁ = (1, 1), g₂ = (1, −½) have product ½, and under θ = diag(½, 2)ψ their transforms have −7/4, while d = (−1, 0) lowers both throughout. The sharp edge: it covers coordinate changes of one parameter space at first order, not function-preserving symmetries or training trajectories ([QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md)). The practice corollary, not to diagnose task conflict by gradient cosine, is the anthology's. | Active |
| [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) v3 | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. When competition between components is mediated by shared resources with feature or niche vectors u_i, so that A = UᵀU and r = Uᵀb − c, the Lotka–Volterra dynamics are ṅ_i = −n_i ∂_i L with L(n) = ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn: entropic mirror descent on the positive orthant. A rare component's invasion fitness is −∂_i L, the value of adding that feature, and uninvadable equilibria are the KKT points of the convex program. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. Mehta et al. (2019) and Marsland, Cui and Mehta (2020) give the general duality for consumer–resource models. | Active |
| [CLAIM-370](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-370.md) | For a symmetric positive-pair distribution with marginal p, the conditional-expectation operator on L²(p) has the density ratio K⁺ as its kernel, and it is Hilbert–Schmidt exactly when the χ²-divergence of the pair from the product of its marginals is finite, in which case it is compact and self-adjoint with an orthonormal eigenbasis | [THEORY-005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md)'s derivation, stated as the record's own and with its proof. Here the condition is exact: Hilbert–Schmidt if and only if finite χ². It says nothing about what trained features span. | Active |
| [CLAIM-371](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-371.md) | Under the componentwise order on distortion profiles, two profiles are incomparable exactly when they trade off, and then positive weightings can rank them either way, while every positive weighting agrees with a dominance | The order-theoretic part of [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md), on its own so that it can carry its own warrant. | [CLAIM-372](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-372.md) | Within a fixed measurement scenario, the contextual fraction is a piecewise-linear and Lipschitz-continuous function of the empirical model's probability table, with a constant that depends only on the scenario | The record's own derivation, from the linear programme of Abramsky, Barbosa and Mansfield ([LIT-265](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md), Eq. 3), which [THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) holds. | [CLAIM-373](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-373.md) | If a map approximately intertwines two operators, with defects E_A = ΦA − A′Φ and E_B = ΦB − B′Φ, then Φ[A,B] − [A′,B′]Φ = A′E_B + E_A B − B′E_A − E_B A, so the commutator is carried to within (‖A‖ + ‖A′‖)‖E_B‖ + (‖B‖ + ‖B′‖)‖E_A‖ | The commutator-distortion identity of the manuscript's §9, on its own and proved. | [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md) v3 | Under one-hop allocation within an epoch, an operator that grants influence to an ally whose policy is nearer its own than the collective decision is raises how far its preferred policy is realized while its own authority stays fixed, so the two conditions of the grant scheme hold together | The demonstrated core of [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md). | [CLAIM-376](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-376.md) v2 | A linear system that is stable at every instant can have a positive Lyapunov exponent: shifting any operator with exponent λ > 0 by −δI lowers its exponent by exactly δ and makes every instantaneous operator stable, so for 0 < δ < λ the shifted system is stable at every instant and unstable | The case [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md)'s source asserts and does not show. | [CLAIM-377](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | For any differentiable model under squared loss with Gaussian noise of precision β, the model's Fisher on n inputs is the Gauss–Newton matrix βJᵀJ, and its non-zero eigenvalues are exactly β times those of the empirical NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ, with the same multiplicities, its eigenvectors being Jᵀ applied to the Gram matrix's, normalized | [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-378](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) v2 | A representational similarity index invariant to every invertible linear map depends on a representation only through its column space, so it takes one value on all column-centred representations of rank n − 1, as it does on all representations of rank n | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. | [CLAIM-379](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-379.md) v2 | On a finite set of stimuli, regularized linear readouts with ridge b > 0 cannot tell apart two centred representations of the same width exactly when one is an orthogonal transformation of the other, and the unregularized CCA member cannot tell apart representations with the same column space, which differ by an invertible linear map | The proved core of [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md).
